Timeline::set_month¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::set_month(int month) const

Move Dates To A Named Month¶

set_month() replaces the local month of every defined timestamp with one numeric month in [1, 12]. Year, day-of-month, time of day, nanoseconds, timezone, and shape are retained.

This method answers a precise calendar-editing need: “keep the day and clock, but place these values in February.” It does not mean “advance to the second month from here,” and it does not mean “move by a month.” Because the original day is retained, the requested month must contain that day.

Example: One Month Across A Matrix¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-15T23:58:59.123456789Z", "2024-06-20T04:05:06.000000004Z"},
    {"2024-09-28T12:30:45.900000000Z", "2024-12-01T00:00:00.000000001Z"},
});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(t.set_month(2), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-02-15T23:58:59.123456789+00:00", "2024-02-20T04:05:06.000000004+00:00"], 
  ["2024-02-28T12:30:45.900000000+00:00", "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000001+00:00"]
]

Rank and layout are preserved logically; this is not a flattening operation. The example also shows that subsecond fields survive unchanged.

Strict Day Compatibility¶

try {
  const auto month_end = pluss::timeline::make("2024-05-31T08:00:00Z");
  (void)month_end.set_month(2);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "day does not exist in requested month\n";
}

Output¶

day does not exist in requested month

There is deliberately no end-of-month clamp. If 31 May becoming February should mean February’s final day in your application, express that policy explicitly before replacement; set_month() will not guess it.

Values outside [1, 12] throw before traversal, including for an empty receiver. If any lane fails day compatibility, no result is returned. NaT lanes remain NaT and do not make an otherwise valid replacement fail.

Replacement Is Not A Month Offset¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make("2024-11-10T09:30:00Z");
std::cout << pluss::timeline::format(t.set_month(2), "%F %T").at(0) << '\n';

Output¶

2024-02-10 09:30:00

The result is February of the same year, not January 2025. This makes set_month() suitable for constructing fixed calendar scenarios, not for measuring or shifting elapsed time.

See Also¶

  • month: inspect the local month number.

  • set_day: replace the day within each retained year and month.
